# Precursor Property

> Independent property due diligence reports for buyers and small developers across Victoria, Australia. We gather the public record on a property (title, planning, sales evidence, market data) and deliver a plain-English report with a clear verdict, before you sign or bid. A$49 flat fee, typically delivered in about 48 hours.

Precursor closes the information gap in a property purchase: the vendor and agent know the covenants, overlays, sale history and real yield; the buyer usually gets a brochure and a fifteen-minute inspection. An automated research pipeline collects the relevant public datasets, and a human analyst reviews every finding, resolves conflicts, and writes the conclusions. Reports are shaped to the property and the client's brief, so sections and depth vary. Precursor is independent: it does not sell property, take referral fees, or earn commission on a purchase.

Precursor provides independent research and analysis, not personal financial, investment, or legal advice.

## Reports

- [Purchase Intelligence](https://www.precursorproperty.com/reports/purchase): Due diligence for buyers and investors. Title and encumbrances, zoning and overlays, comparable sales, rental yield, capital growth signals, vendor intelligence, negotiation strategy. One report: Full Due Diligence, A$49 flat.
- [Development Intelligence](https://www.precursorproperty.com/reports/development): Feasibility for owners and small developers. Zoning and residential code, subdivision potential, overlay constraints, permit pathway. Scoped by enquiry: free to enquire, fixed quote within one business day.
- [Pricing](https://www.precursorproperty.com/pricing): A$49 flat, no subscription. Money-back guarantee on a first order.
- [Sample report](https://www.precursorproperty.com/sample-report.html): A complete, real Full Due Diligence report (Montmorency VIC), republished with permission and with identifying details withheld.

## About

- [Our Method](https://www.precursorproperty.com/method): Why Precursor exists, the primary data sources used (VicPlan, Landata, council records, licensed sales data), and the honest boundary that reports are desktop research, not physical inspections.
- [FAQ](https://www.precursorproperty.com/faq): How reports differ from a building inspection or conveyancer, how a full report costs A$49, turnaround, data sources, confidentiality, and how each report adapts to the property.
- [Order a report](https://www.precursorproperty.com/order): Two-step order form; payment via Stripe. Development enquiries use the same form with no payment.

## Insights (guides)

- [Five Victorian suburbs to watch for the rest of 2026, and how each could disappoint you](https://www.precursorproperty.com/blog/victorian-suburbs-to-watch-2026): Kurunjang, Hampton, Mount Helen, North Bendigo and the Stage 2 activity centres, with REIV June quarter 2026 data, the planning decisions behind each, and the failure mode of each pick.
- [Investors are pulling out of Victorian property. Is this your window?](https://www.precursorproperty.com/blog/investor-exodus-victoria-2026): Investor loan applications fell around 20% after the May 2026 budget's proposed negative gearing and CGT changes. What a thinner market gives buyers, and the three traps inside it.
- [Why one in five Melbourne apartment resales loses money](https://www.precursorproperty.com/blog/melbourne-apartment-resale-losses-2026): Unit prices fell less than houses in 2026, but Melbourne apartment resales turn a profit far less often than houses. Land share, supply, owners corporation costs and the off-the-plan premium.
- [Melbourne falls, regional Victoria runs: the mid-2026 divide](https://www.precursorproperty.com/blog/melbourne-vs-regional-victoria-2026): June 2026 data has Melbourne values falling while regional Victorian medians set records. Drivers, buyer leverage, and the regional traps.
- [Three rate rises in 2026: stress-testing a Victorian purchase](https://www.precursorproperty.com/blog/rising-rates-victorian-buyers-2026): The 4.35% cash rate, the 11 August RBA decision, what each 25 basis points costs, and how to stress-test before signing.
- [Property tax & budget changes for Victorian investors in 2026](https://www.precursorproperty.com/blog/victorian-property-tax-changes-2026): Negative gearing (proposed), the foreign-buyer ban, land tax, VRLT, and the short-stay and ESVF levies. What is law and what is not.
- [Victoria's 2026 rental reforms](https://www.precursorproperty.com/blog/victoria-rental-reforms-2026): No-fault evictions abolished, 90-day rent notices, minimum standards, portable bonds, and a proposed rent freeze.
- [Victorian property capital growth in 2026](https://www.precursorproperty.com/blog/victoria-capital-growth-2026): Current medians, divergent bank forecasts, and the corridors growing 6 to 10 percent while the average sits near 2.
- [Zoning explained for Victorian buyers](https://www.precursorproperty.com/blog/zoning-explained-for-victorian-buyers): NRZ, GRZ, RGZ, the 2025 reforms, and what decides whether you can build or subdivide.
- [Planning overlays in Victoria](https://www.precursorproperty.com/blog/planning-overlays-victoria-explained): Flood, bushfire and heritage overlays that can restrict a build even in a good zone.
- [Section 32 red flags](https://www.precursorproperty.com/blog/section-32-red-flags-victoria): Easements, owners-corporation debts, unpermitted works and outstanding charges to check in a vendor statement.
